record.original_question: For every natural number k, are there infinitely many primes p such that p+2k is also prime?

evidence.quote: In 1849, de Polignac proposed a more general conjecture that, for every natural number k, there are infinitely many primes p such that p+2k is a prime.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$ denote the set of natural numbers, and let $\mathcal{P} = \{2, 3, 5, 7, 11, \ldots\}$ denote the set of prime numbers. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, decide whether the set $\{p \in \mathcal{P} : p + 2k \in \mathcal{P}\}$ is infinite. Equivalently, prove or disprove: for every natural number $k$, there exist infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 2k$ is also prime.
artifact.status_search_result: This is de Polignac's conjecture (1849); the case $k=1$ is the twin prime conjecture. It remains open for every individual $k$. Zhang (2013), Maynard, and the Polymath8 project established that there exist infinitely many prime pairs differing by some bounded even number (currently at most 246), but no specific value of $2k$ has been proven to occur infinitely often.

status_evidence.title: Polignac's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In number theory, Polignac's conjecture was made by Alphonse de Polignac in 1849... For n = 1 it is the twin prime conjecture. The conjecture has not been proved or disproven for any specific value of n.
status_evidence.claim: De Polignac's conjecture remains unproven for every natural number k.

status_evidence.title: Bounded gaps between primes - Yitang Zhang
status_evidence.snippet: It is proved that liminf (p_{n+1}-p_n) is finite, with an explicit bound.
status_evidence.claim: Bounded prime gaps are known to occur infinitely often, but no specific gap 2k has been shown to occur infinitely often.
